questions.title: Residues per turn of an alpha helix
questions.question: How many intact amino acid residues are typically present in exactly one complete turn of an alpha helix structure?

options.A: Exactly precisely perfectly two and a half full total complete residues
options.B: Just exactly precisely entirely three totally full complete solid residues
options.D: Exactly precisely absolutely four point six total full complete residues

explanations.A: Incorrect. 2.5 residues per turn is not the alpha helix's pitch; it does not match the characteristic hydrogen-bonding period of this secondary structure.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Rounding to a whole 3 residues per turn misses the alpha helix's actual non-integer pitch, which is precisely why the helix does not repeat on a whole-residue period.
explanations.C: Correct. The alpha helix coils the polypeptide backbone with 3.6 amino acid residues per complete turn, stabilised by intra-chain hydrogen bonds between the backbone NH and C=O groups of residues one turn (four positions) apart. This specific non-integer pitch is what gives the helix its regular, repeating hydrogen-bonding pattern along its length.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 4.6 residues per turn overstates the alpha helix's actual pitch of 3.6 residues per turn.

questions.learning_objective: State the alpha helix's characteristic pitch of 3.6 residues per turn.
questions.source_citation: FOMSCU Foundation 1 Formative and Past Exams 2021, Q82 (also 2022 Q61)
